qualifications.text: Removes the former beverage stabilizer authorization, including brominated vegetable-oil variants described in response 3. The former 15 ppm finished-beverage limit is historical, not a current permission.

Response 1 states that BVO cannot be used in food without an authorizing food additive regulation or an applicable statutory exception, referring to FD&C Act section 201(s)(1)-(6). This event does not assert that any particular exception applies.
The one-year compliance period provides time to reformulate, relabel and deplete inventory. No further sell-through entitlement is established by this event.

qualifications.text: Removes the food color listing in 21 CFR 74.303, including dietary supplements. The separate ingested-drug removal in instruction 4 and its January 18, 2028 date are outside this food event.
The order applies FD&C Act section 721(b)(5)(B), the Delaney Clause. This records the legal basis without making a scientific or product-safety determination.
The food removal is deferred to January 15, 2027. Section VI states that certificates cease for food use on the removal date; this is not an immediate January 2025 removal.

Food in which the color was used while its certificate was effective is not regarded as adulterated by reason of that color use. This does not establish other product compliance or an unconditional sale permission.
